availableCommands.name: google-workspace
availableCommands.description: Read this before the first Google Drive, Docs, Sheets or Slides connector call whenever the task creates or changes a Google file. Use this skill whenever the user wants to create or change a Google Doc, Sheet or Slides file in their Google Drive. Triggers include: a request that names Google Docs, Sheets, Slides or Drive and asks to make, edit, format, copy or rename a file; a docs.google.com link with a request to change that file, even a one-line fix or suggested edits; and any follow-up change to a Google file from earlier in the chat, even "change it" or "add a tab". Includes helper scripts for document positions, cell ranges and slide layout. However, if the user asks for a doc, deck or spreadsheet without naming Google, or gives a Google file only as source material for something new, use Claude's own output type instead. Do NOT use for read-only questions about a Google file, or for Word, Excel, PowerPoint or PDF files.

---
10→# D21 — одно итоговое review всей работы P2.2 + P2.3

**Actor:** владелец репозитория, текущая Codex-сессия.
**Evidence:** прямое уточнение владельца в текущем root:
> а почему нельзя было сделать все в одно ревью?????????? так в инструкциях написано
> что ревью должен быть по всей работе, а не по кускам

SHA-256 двух дословных сообщений, соединённых LF: `87e85459bae03f9fdf56651f632ec7623706a6761a474405460c6202f375b94c`.

## Solution
20→
Единица итогового независимого Grok review — весь исходно заказанный workset
P2.2 + P2.3. Реализация исходного P2.3 включается в ещё открытый P2.2; все его
исходные требования и исключения сохранены дословно в
`artifacts/P2.2/combined-review-unit/P2.3-original.md`. Исходный P2.2 сохранён
в `artifacts/P2.2/combined-review-unit/P2.2-original.md`. Оба результата,
новые и удалённые файлы, необходимые нормы, зависимости и финальное validation
передаются вместе в одну отдельную read-only сессию. История executor туда не
передаётся. Selector остаётся `grok/grok-4.7/500k`, effort high.

30→Владелец изменил организацию review, а не условия приёмки. Полный обязательный
набор обоих исходных пунктов исполняется на стабильном объединённом кандидате;
после GREEN обязательны freshness и closure checks. История P2.2, текущие
attempt 5 / run `08750714b29a6d5a7792f308c7e281d3832ed1f76f0f1b29319a02f60f1c124b`,
подлинный FINDINGS первого completed review и бюджет двух completed rounds
сохраняются. Остановленная по уточнению владельца вторая transport attempt
сохраняется как INCOMPLETE, не становится GREEN и не обнуляет бюджет.

P2.3 после реального закрытия объединённого P2.2 — successor verification:
проверяет выполненные исходные обязанности documents и подлинную поставку
40→общего review. Отдельный reviewer request P2.3 не создаётся; это явная отмена
per-item автоматизации исходного selector для этого successor, поскольку тот
же весь продукт уже входит в общий reviewer unit. Его старт и закрытие
выполняются существующими native admission, contract, recovery и terminal API,
с исходным root invocation и фактической route evidence. Подмена item_id в
review receipt или копирование чужого GREEN запрещены.

## Why

Уточнение владельца требует review всей заказанной работы. Coalescence сохраняет
50→последовательную native зависимость P2.2 → P2.3 и все требования продукта,
при этом не требует второго частичного review или изменения Task runtime.
Будущие пункты, схемы/колонки P4.1, Types/Content/export и push/publication
не включаются.

## Executable acceptance mapping

The exact original P2.2 and P2.3 acceptance literals remain mandatory in their
immutable `combined-review-unit/P2.2-original.md` and `P2.3-original.md` archives.
Executable carriers change transport, preserving every obligation:
60→
- `code-guidance`: both original Code Guidance gates, actual reflection and E10 zero-hit.
- `packages-pg`: actual four-package Pint/PHPStan/Pest, completed generation, exact isolated P1 PostgreSQL matrices with zero failed/skipped, unchanged candidate and runtime.
- `drive-arch`: original drive Arch/Providers gate and its actual counts.
- `documents-arch`: original documents Arch/Providers gate and its actual counts.
- `combined-review`: authentic independent entire-workset P2.2 Grok GREEN for current bytes.
- `producer-delivery`: committed native P2.2 close and its authentic entire-workset GREEN, with current product equality; no P2.3 review relabel or request.
- `freshness`: current P2.3 native item/bundle/decisions/status checks and selected lint before close; native terminal reconciliation and terminal delivery remain mandatory after close.

The behavioral DAG and its stable evidence precede the direct native review
70→packet. The packet binds those receipts/logs and acceptance code/config. After
actual GREEN, lightweight executable qualification runs through the current
contract, followed by native closure. Qualification output is outside the reviewed
inventory and does not rewrite behavioral or review evidence.

The active Vue type comment referencing the removed document resource is updated mechanically to `DocumentRevisionResource`; TypeScript types and behavior remain unchanged. This satisfies original P2.3 Code Guidance over package source callers.

**Evidence:** после предъявления `findings/P2.2-handle-contract-conflict.md` и двух
вариантов владелец поручил: «выстраивай как правильно, последовательность мне не
важна, важен финальный результат».

Исполнитель выбирает второй предъявленный вариант: включить в P2.2 минимальную
20→смену двух методов интерфейса `packages/core/src/Contracts/Drive/DriveHandle.php`
и необходимых callers, чтобы полностью выполнить исходный результат P2.2:
`storage(): Drive` → `model(): Drive`, `panel(): string` → `profile(): Profile`.
Реализация возвращает зарегистрированный Profile через существующий
ProfileRegistry. Golden, UPGRADE и CHANGELOG обновляются в том же item.
Временные обёртки не добавляются; остальной объём P3.2 остаётся отдельным.

Удаление неиспользуемого WorkspaceRef включает удаление его orphan unit-test
в core: этот тест проверяет только удаляемый класс. HTTP Requests размещаются
по существующим доменам Folders/Files/Nodes без смены коротких имён.
30→
P2.2 и P2.3 исполняются в текущем root с Grok review и исходной Validation.
Публичные entry points Vaulter::for/forStorage, остальные методы handle,
поведение маршрутов и JSON не меняются. Push/publication не разрешаются.

## Why

Одновременная смена интерфейса и реализации сохраняет типизированный seam и
устраняет воспроизведённый PHP fatal. Она выполняет исходный результат P2.2 без
переходного API и не требует реализации будущих Operations/Actor-контрактов.

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace Vaulter\Contracts\Drive;

use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Collection;
use Vaulter\Models\Drive\Drive;
use Vaulter\Models\Drive\Node;
use Vaulter\Profiles\Profile;

/**
 * The ergonomic Drive handle bound to one (Storage, panel) — the surface
 * `Vaulter::for($entity)` / `Vaulter::forStorage($storage)` returns (§2.1).
 *
 * The contract lives in core (the kernel owns the Node/Storage models and the
 * public facade entry point) while the concrete handle ships in vaulter-drive
 * (P2 #5 / ADR-0015): core defines what a handle CAN do, the drive package binds
 * the implementation. A host that has not installed vaulter-drive still type-hints
 * against this interface; resolving it fails loudly with an install hint.
 */
interface DriveHandle
{
    public function model(): Drive;

    public function profile(): Profile;

    /**
     * The storage's root folder node (§2.1).
     */
    public function root(): Node;

    public function createFolder(string $name, ?Node $parent = null, int|string|null $actorId = null): Node;

    /**
     * Upload bytes into the Drive (§2.4). $source may be a PSR StreamInterface, an
     * SplFileInfo / UploadedFile, an open stream resource, or a raw string.
     */
    public function upload(
        mixed $source,
        ?Node $into = null,
        ?string $name = null,
        ?string $mimeType = null,
        ?string $originalName = null,
        int|string|null $actorId = null,
    ): Node;

    /**
     * Upload a NEW VERSION onto an existing file node (§2.4).
     */
    public function uploadVersion(
        Node $target,
        mixed $source,
        ?string $mimeType = null,
        ?string $originalName = null,
        int|string|null $actorId = null,
    ): Node;

    public function move(Node $node, ?Node $into = null, int|string|null $actorId = null): Node;

    public function rename(Node $node, string $name, int|string|null $actorId = null): Node;

    public function copy(Node $node, ?Node $into = null, ?string $name = null, int|string|null $actorId = null): Node;

    public function trash(Node $node, int|string|null $actorId = null): Node;

    public function restore(Node $node, int|string|null $actorId = null): Node;

    public function forceDelete(Node $node, int|string|null $actorId = null): void;

    /**
     * Direct children of a folder (or the root when null) — the hot listing.
     *
     * @return Collection<int, Node>
     */
    public function list(?Node $folder = null): Collection;
}

 * the surface `Vaulter::for($entity)` returns. Every method is a thin delegation
 * to a final readonly Action (write) or NodeReadRepository (read); the handle adds
 * no business logic, only the convenience of a pre-resolved storage + the
 * stream-normalisation that keeps the Actions free of HTTP/PSR types.
 *
 * Authorization (M2a / H.2) is enforced at the HTTP controller boundary
 * (NodeController + AccessResolver) before these methods are reached — the handle
 * itself stays a pure delegation surface and performs no access checks, mirroring
 * the legacy DocumentVisibilityService placement canon.

    public function model(): Drive
    {
        return $this->storage;
    }

    public function profile(): Profile
    {
        return $this->profiles->get($this->storage->profile);
    }

    /**
     * The storage's root folder node (§2.1).
     */
    public function root(): Node
    {
        return $this->storages->root($this->storage);
    }

    public function createFolder(string $name, ?Node $parent = null, int|string|null $actorId = null): Node
    {
        return $this->createFolder->execute(new CreateFolderInput(
            storage: $this->storage,
            name: $name,
            parent: $parent ?? $this->root(),
            actorId: $actorId,
        ));
    }

     * $into is the destination folder (null = root); $name overrides the stored
     * name. Typed mixed so core need not hard-require psr/http-message.
     */
    public function upload(
        mixed $source,
        ?Node $into = null,
        ?string $name = null,
        ?string $mimeType = null,
        ?string $originalName = null,
        int|string|null $actorId = null,

        $stream = $this->toStream($source);
        $resolvedOriginalName = $originalName ?? $this->originalNameFor($source) ?? ($name ?? 'upload.bin');

            storage: $this->storage,

            mimeType: $mimeType ?? $this->mimeTypeFor($source),
            into: $into ?? $this->root(),
            name: $name,
            actorId: $actorId,
        ));
    }

139→def green(plan, root, config, *, committed=False):
140→    item = config['producer_item']
    if committed:
        from task import terminal_policy
        event = plan_item_state.material_terminal_evidence(plan, item)
        need(event['result'] == 'closed-green', 'combined producer not closed GREEN')
        terminal_policy.validate_predecessor(event['decision'], result=event['result'], plan_dir=plan, item_id=item)
        receipt = review_packet.require_committed_green(plan, item, config['reviewer'],
                  effort=config['review_effort'], decision=event['decision'], result=event['result'])
    else:
        receipt = review_packet.require_green(plan, item, config['reviewer'], effort=config['review_effort'])
150→    manifest = receipt['manifest']
    need(review_packet._members(root, manifest['paths']) == manifest['snapshot']['product'],
         'current product differs from authentic entire-workset review')
    need(config['consumer_item'] not in {manifest['item_id']}, 'producer review relabeled as consumer')

availableCommands.name: google-workspace
availableCommands.description: Read this before the first Google Drive, Docs, Sheets or Slides connector call whenever the task creates or changes a Google file. Use this skill whenever the user wants to create or change a Google Doc, Sheet or Slides file in their Google Drive. Triggers include: a request that names Google Docs, Sheets, Slides or Drive and asks to make, edit, format, copy or rename a file; a docs.google.com link with a request to change that file, even a one-line fix or suggested edits; and any follow-up change to a Google file from earlier in the chat, even "change it" or "add a tab". Includes helper scripts for document positions, cell ranges and slide layout. However, if the user asks for a doc, deck or spreadsheet without naming Google, or gives a Google file only as source material for something new, use Claude's own output type instead. Do NOT use for read-only questions about a Google file, or for Word, Excel, PowerPoint or PDF files.

availableCommands.name: user:docs
availableCommands.description: docs (editable docs people share and comment on; the default for any document, named as a doc or not: a document, report, proposal, resume, cover letter, letter, contract, policy, form, template, worksheet, essay, handbook, guide, how-to, cheat sheet, SOP or other writing to keep, share, collaborate on, send, submit, print or sign; a doc exports to Word, PDF, Markdown or Google Docs, so needing a file to send, attach, upload, submit or print is no reason to pick Word, and a file nobody asked for is a doc, not Word; a plan, comparison, summary or notes asked in chat stays in chat; a pasted claude.ai artifact link may be a doc: check with docs tools first; Word or another file format named, tracked changes wanted, or a .docx to change or use as a template → that format's skill): making one → if no docs-connector instructions are in context, call its `guide` (topic.instructions) first; then create the doc (headings only, no body) before any search, file read or plan, even with files attached.

availableCommands.name: google-workspace
availableCommands.description: Read this before the first Google Drive, Docs, Sheets or Slides connector call whenever the task creates or changes a Google file. Use this skill whenever the user wants to create or change a Google Doc, Sheet or Slides file in their Google Drive. Triggers include: a request that names Google Docs, Sheets, Slides or Drive and asks to make, edit, format, copy or rename a file; a docs.google.com link with a request to change that file, even a one-line fix or suggested edits; and any follow-up change to a Google file from earlier in the chat, even "change it" or "add a tab". Includes helper scripts for document positions, cell ranges and slide layout. However, if the user asks for a doc, deck or spreadsheet without naming Google, or gives a Google file only as source material for something new, use Claude's own output type instead. Do NOT use for read-only questions about a Google file, or for Word, Excel, PowerPoint or PDF files.

availableCommands.name: bundled:review
availableCommands.description: Run a reviewer subagent against your whole branch vs main, your uncommitted working state, a named branch, a single GitHub PR, or an entire Graphite/stacked-PR stack (one reviewer subagent per PR). use Illuminate\Routing\Middleware\SubstituteBindings;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Route;
use Vaulter\Documents\Http\Controllers\Collaboration\NodeCollaborationController;
use Vaulter\Documents\Http\Controllers\Comments\NodeCommentController;
use Vaulter\Documents\Http\Controllers\Documents\DocumentNodeController;
use Vaulter\Documents\Http\Middleware\ResolveCollaborationCall;
use Vaulter\Http\Middleware\ResolveVaulterRouteParameters;
use Vaulter\Support\Config;

/*
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------
| Vaulter Documents API routes (P2 #5 / ADR-0015, D2)
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------
| The document-node surface, extracted from core's routes/api.php into the
| vaulter-documents package. Mounted under the SAME configured prefix (default:
| api/vaulter) and middleware as the kernel routes — Laravel merges the group
| registrations across files. Local resource middleware resolves {storage} and
| {node} through swappable core repositories before SubstituteBindings. The fixed sub-segments (content/versions/handler/export/collab/
| comments) differ in segment count from core's and vaulter-drive's catch-all
| /{node}, so cross-file registration order never shadows them.
*/

Route::prefix(Config::routePrefix())
    ->middleware(Config::authenticatedMiddleware())
    ->group(static function (): void {
        Route::middleware([ResolveVaulterRouteParameters::class, SubstituteBindings::class])->group(static function (): void {
            /*
            |------------------------------------------------------------------
            | Documents — document nodes (§2.5 / §7 / M4a)
            |------------------------------------------------------------------
            | Create a kind=document node, read/autosave its content, snapshot
            | named versions, restore a prior version, resolve its handler
            | descriptor and export it. Gated on the 'document_versions' feature
            | (the v_node_document_versions schema). Authorized via the
            | AccessResolver (Create on the destination, View to read, Edit to
            | write).
            */
            if (Config::featureEnabled('document_versions')) {
                Route::post('storages/{storage}/documents', [DocumentNodeController::class, 'store']);

                Route::get('nodes/{node}/content', [DocumentNodeController::class, 'content']);
                Route::patch('nodes/{node}/content', [DocumentNodeController::class, 'update']);
                Route::get('nodes/{node}/document-versions', [DocumentNodeController::class, 'versions']);
                Route::post('nodes/{node}/document-versions', [DocumentNodeController::class, 'storeVersion']);
                Route::post('nodes/{node}/document-versions/{version}/restore', [DocumentNodeController::class, 'restore']);
                // Release a keep_forever pin (F-P1.12-03) — the missing inverse of
                // the pin `storeVersion` can set; the version re-enters the prune
                // window on the node's next snapshot/restore.
                Route::patch('nodes/{node}/document-versions/{version}/keep-forever', [DocumentNodeController::class, 'releaseVersion']);
                Route::get('nodes/{node}/handler', [DocumentNodeController::class, 'handler']);
                Route::get('nodes/{node}/export', [DocumentNodeController::class, 'export']);
            }

            // Realtime collaboration connect handshake (§7 / ADR-0001 / M4b):
            // authorized via the AccessResolver (≥ View/Comment to connect, read-only
            // unless Edit), returning the transport-agnostic CollaborationSession
            // descriptor. Gated on BOTH 'document_versions' (the schema the session
            // reads/writes against) AND 'collaboration' (VLT-REMED P3.1 / F-P1.6-01,
            // D13/D20) — the realtime surface is a SEPARATE opt-in over base
            // (non-realtime) document editing, not implied by it.
            if (Config::featureEnabled('document_versions') && Config::collaborationEnabled()) {
                Route::post('nodes/{node}/collab/token', [NodeCollaborationController::class, 'token']);
            }

            // NODE-attached comments (ADR-0014 шаг 1) — the additive twin of the
            // legacy document_id-bound comments. Gated on the 'comments' feature.
            // Authorized via AccessResolver: read ≥ View, create = Comment, resolve/
            // delete = the AUTHOR or Manage. {comment} is a plain scalar (the model is
            // swappable, not route-model bound) — the controller resolves it and
            // asserts it belongs to the bound node.
            if (Config::featureEnabled('comments')) {
                Route::get('nodes/{node}/comments', [NodeCommentController::class, 'index']);
                Route::post('nodes/{node}/comments', [NodeCommentController::class, 'store']);
                Route::post('nodes/{node}/comments/{comment}/resolve', [NodeCommentController::class, 'resolve']);
                Route::delete('nodes/{node}/comments/{comment}', [NodeCommentController::class, 'destroy']);

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace Vaulter\Documents\Providers;

use Illuminate\Contracts\Config\Repository;
use Illuminate\Support\ServiceProvider;
use Symfony\Component\HtmlSanitizer\HtmlSanitizer;
use Symfony\Component\HtmlSanitizer\HtmlSanitizerConfig;
use Symfony\Component\HtmlSanitizer\HtmlSanitizerInterface;
use Vaulter\Documents\Contracts\ExportFilenameResolver;
use Vaulter\Documents\Engines\Handlers\UniverHandler;
use Vaulter\Documents\Export\DefaultExportFilenameResolver;

final class BindingsRegistrar extends ServiceProvider
{
    public function register(): void
    {
        $config = $this->app->make(Repository::class);

        // Own the node-comment / document-version swappable-model defaults and
        // contribute the TipTap handler + built-in exporters WITHOUT changing the
        // config paths hosts use: merge them under the existing `vaulter.models` /
        // `vaulter.handlers` / `vaulter.exporters` keys. Core ships its OWN
        // `vaulter.handlers` baseline (PreviewHandler/DownloadOnlyHandler, P0.4/D10)
        // and no defaults for models/exporters — this merge ADDS TipTapHandler
        // alongside the core baseline; a host's own config still wins on key overlap
        // (array_merge, host second) — the drive/media provider precedent.
        //
        // Cache-safety (F-P2.2-01, D19): a single config file back three DIFFERENT
        // top-level `vaulter.*` keys, so a plain `mergeConfigFrom($path, 'vaulter.models')`
        // is not viable here — it would merge the WHOLE returned array (models +
        // handlers + exporters) under `vaulter.models`, mis-nesting the latter two.
        // The merge is instead gated the same way `mergeConfigFrom` gates itself
        // (`configurationIsCached()`): when the host has run `config:cache`, the
        // merged values are already baked into the cached config, so re-reading the
        // file from disk and recomputing the merge on every request is redundant I/O
        // in `register()` (`.claude/rules/service-provider.md`).
        if (!$this->app->configurationIsCached()) {
            /** @var array{models: array<string, class-string>, handlers: list<class-string>, exporters: array<string, class-string>} $defaults */
            $defaults = require __DIR__.'/../../config/vaulter-documents.php';

            /** @var array<string, class-string> $existingModels */
            $existingModels = $config->get('vaulter.models', []);
            /** @var list<class-string> $existingHandlers */
            $existingHandlers = $config->get('vaulter.handlers', []);
            /** @var array<string, class-string> $existingExporters */
            $existingExporters = $config->get('vaulter.exporters', []);

            $config->set([
                'vaulter.models' => array_merge($defaults['models'], $existingModels),
                'vaulter.handlers' => array_merge($defaults['handlers'], $existingHandlers),
                'vaulter.exporters' => array_merge($defaults['exporters'], $existingExporters),
            ]);
        }

        // The feature-flagged UniverHandler is added to the tagged 'vaulter.handlers'
        // set ONLY when the 'spreadsheets' feature is on, so a stock install never
        // resolves xlsx to it (xlsx then falls to DownloadOnly). The format-
        // extensibility registry engine itself (`Vaulter\Handlers\FileHandlerRegistry`)
        // and the `NodePresenter` seam now bind in core (P0.4/D10) — this
        // package only ever ADDS handlers to it, never owns the engine.
        if ($config->get('vaulter.features.spreadsheets', false) === true) {
            $this->app->tag([UniverHandler::class], 'vaulter.file_handlers');
        }

        // The export filename seam (P4.5 / F-P3.1-04): NodeExportService stays
        // `final` (H.5 arch gate), so a host wanting a different export filename
        // scheme rebinds this contract to its own class instead of forking the
        // service. Bound to the pre-P4.5 hardcoded scheme (node basename + exporter
        // extension) — default behaviour is unchanged.
        $this->app->bind(ExportFilenameResolver::class, DefaultExportFilenameResolver::class);

        // Second echelon of the F-P1.11-01 stored-XSS fix (D4): TipTapRenderer takes
        // the sanitizer through its constructor (never resolved inline from the
        // container) so every HTML render — including content persisted before the
        // store-time validator existed — is sanitized on the way out. Singleton: the
        // sanitizer is stateless and config-immutable per request.
        $this->app->singleton(HtmlSanitizerInterface::class, static function (): HtmlSanitizer {
            $config = (new HtmlSanitizerConfig)
                ->allowSafeElements()
                ->allowLinkSchemes(['https', 'http', 'mailto'])
                ->allowMediaSchemes(['https', 'http']);

            return new HtmlSanitizer($config);
        });
    }
}

namespace Vaulter\Drive\Providers;

use Illuminate\Support\ServiceProvider;
use Vaulter\Contracts\Drive\DriveHandleFactory as DriveHandleFactoryContract;
use Vaulter\Drive\DriveHandleFactory;
use Vaulter\Drive\DriveProvisioner;
use Vaulter\Drive\Uploads\UploadSessionManager;

final class BindingsRegistrar extends ServiceProvider
{
    public function register(): void
    {
        $this->mergeConfigFrom(__DIR__.'/../../config/vaulter-drive.php', 'vaulter.models');

        $this->app->bind(DriveHandleFactoryContract::class, DriveHandleFactory::class);
        $this->app->singleton(DriveProvisioner::class);
        $this->app->singleton(UploadSessionManager::class);
    }
}

namespace Vaulter\Documents\Models\Revisions;

use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Model;

use Vaulter\Models\Concerns\ResolvesVaulterConnection;
use Vaulter\Models\Drive\Node;
use Vaulter\Support\Config;

/**
 * An append-only snapshot of a DOCUMENT NODE's content (master plan §2.5 / M4a) —
 * the NEW node-attached document-version path. It is DISTINCT from the legacy
 * {@see DocumentVersion} (document_id-attached, the v_documents path that stays
 * intact); this one hangs off a kind=document {@see Node} via node_id and lives in
 * v_node_document_versions.
 *
 * Append-only (no updated_at / no soft-delete): a committed version is immutable;
 * the autosave HEAD is the one exception the Action overwrites in place within the
 * debounce window. version_no is monotonic per node (the unique index is the
 * backbone). The TipTap JSON projection lives in `content`; the binary Yjs CRDT
 * state (the M4b collaboration source of truth) in `yjs_state`.
 *
 * @property int|string                $id
 * @property int|string|null           $tenant_id
 * @property int|string                $node_id
 * @property int                       $version_no
 * @property array<string, mixed>|null $content
 * @property string|null               $yjs_state
 * @property int|null                  $yjs_state_size
 * @property string                    $format
 * @property string|null               $content_hash
 * @property string|null               $snapshot_label
 * @property bool                      $is_autosave
 * @property string                    $status
 * @property bool                      $keep_forever
 * @property int|string|null           $created_by
 * @property Carbon|null               $created_at
 * @property-read Node $node
 */
class DocumentRevision extends Model
{
    use HasExtraData;
    use HasVaulterKeys;
    use ResolvesVaulterConnection;

    public const UPDATED_AT = null;

    /**
     * Closed allow-list (F-P1.8-02): the version's own document content/label.
     * id/tenant_id/node_id/version_no/yjs_state/yjs_state_size/content_hash/
     * status/created_by are structural/server-computed — every write path that
     * sets them already uses forceFill() (DocumentRevisionStoreRepository).
     *
     * @var list<string>
     */
    protected $fillable = [
        'content',
        'format',
        'snapshot_label',
        'is_autosave',
        'keep_forever',
    ];

    #[\Override]
    public function getTable(): string
    {
        return Config::table('node_document_versions');
    }

    /**
     * @return BelongsTo<Node, $this>
     */
    public function node(): BelongsTo
    {
        return $this->belongsTo(Config::nodeModel(), 'node_id');
    }

    /**
     * The TipTap content of this version (the structural JSON projection).
     *
     * READING NEVER THROWS (VLT-REMED D29 / R-01). A snapshot written before today's
     * allow-list existed — or by a host extension since switched off — DECAYS: unknown
     * nodes/marks/attribute keys are stripped and a valid doc comes back. Store-time
     * validation is the strict gate ({@see TipTapContent::fromArray()}); making the read
     * path equally strict meant a single legacy document threw on preview, export and in
     * the listing UI, i.e. an XSS barrier bought at the price of denial of service.
     *
     * Attribute VALUES survive the decay by design: a legacy `href="javascript:…"` reaches
     * the RENDERER, where the render-time HTML sanitizer (second echelon, D4) neutralises
     * it — that is the echelon's only real input.

availableCommands.name: bundled:review
availableCommands.description: Run a reviewer subagent against your whole branch vs main, your uncommitted working state, a named branch, a single GitHub PR, or an entire Graphite/stacked-PR stack (one reviewer subagent per PR). A bare /review defaults to reviewing your uncommitted working state when the tree is dirty, or your whole branch vs main when the tree is clean. Main, local, and branch modes write a review file plus a summary to disk. PR and stack modes post the findings as a PENDING GitHub review for the user to inspect and submit through the UI. Use --main for an explicit clean-tree branch review, --stack for stacked PRs, --submit to publish immediately as COMMENT, or --approve to publish and approve; the default remains PENDING.

90→## Drive — `Vaulter\Drive\Events` (requires `axioma-studio/vaulter-drive`)

All `ShouldDispatchAfterCommit`.

| Event | Constructor payload |
|---|---|
| `Drives\DriveCreated` | `Drive $storage, Node $root, int\|string\|null $actorId = null, ?string $eventId = null` |
| `Nodes\FolderCreated` | `Node $node, int\|string\|null $actorId = null, ?string $eventId = null` |
| `Files\FileUploaded` | `Node $node, File $file, FileRevision $version, int\|string\|null $actorId = null, ?string $eventId = null` |
| `Files\FileRevisionAdded` | `Node $node, File $file, FileRevision $version, int $versionNo, int\|string\|null $actorId = null, ?string $eventId = null` |
100→| `Nodes\NodeRenamed` | `Node $node, string $fromName, string $toName, int\|string\|null $actorId = null, ?string $eventId = null` |
| `Nodes\NodeMoved` | `Node $node, int\|string\|null $fromParentId, int\|string\|null $toParentId, int\|string\|null $actorId = null, ?string $eventId = null` |
| `Nodes\NodeCopied` | `Node $source, Node $copy, int\|string\|null $actorId = null, ?string $eventId = null` |
| `Nodes\NodeTrashed` | `Node $node, int\|string\|null $actorId = null, ?string $eventId = null` |
| `Nodes\NodeRestored` | `Node $node, int\|string\|null $actorId = null, ?string $eventId = null` |
| `Nodes\NodePurged` | `int\|string $storageId, array $nodeIds, int $freedBytes, int\|string\|null $actorId = null, ?string $eventId = null` |

- `Drives\DriveCreated` — fires when `Vaulter::for()` get-or-creates a `v_storages` row;
  `$root` is the auto-provisioned root folder node.
- `Nodes\NodePurged` — note this carries **ids**, not models (`$storageId`,
110→  `array $nodeIds`) plus `$freedBytes`; it's emitted after the subtree is gone, so its
  rows no longer exist. Listeners can schedule GC and release quota.

## Sharing — `Vaulter\Events\Sharing`

All `ShouldDispatchAfterCommit`.

| Event | Constructor payload |
|---|---|
| `NodeShareCreated` | `NodeShare $share, int\|string\|null $actorId = null` |
120→| `NodeShareRevoked` | `NodeShare $share, int\|string\|null $actorId = null` |

- `NodeShare*` — the **bearer node share-link** channel (`v_node_shares`); this is the
  only sharing channel Vaulter ships today (see [ADR-0013](/adr/0013-two-sharing-channels)).

See [Usage → Sharing](/guide/sharing).

## Reliability note
130→
When `features.reliability` is on, an after-commit subscriber (the `OutboxRecorder`)
stages domain events into `v_outbox` in the same request as the mutation; the
`vaulter:relay-outbox` command then fans each row out into signed webhook deliveries.
Consumers must **dedupe on the `event_id`** carried in the payload — the outbox is
idempotent by `event_id`, but a delivery may be re-queued. See
[Recipes → Reliability & webhooks](/guide/recipes).

## See also

140→- [Commands reference](/reference/commands) — the relay/retry/GC schedulables
- [Configuration reference](/reference/configuration) — `features.reliability`, `collaboration.channel_prefix`, `webhooks.*`
- [Contracts reference](/reference/contracts) — the models these payloads carry

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace Vaulter\Documents\Events\Comments;

use Illuminate\Broadcasting\Channel;
use Illuminate\Broadcasting\PrivateChannel;
use Illuminate\Contracts\Broadcasting\ShouldBroadcast;
use Illuminate\Support\Str;
use Vaulter\Documents\Models\Comments\NodeComment;
use Vaulter\Support\Config;
use Vaulter\Support\Identity;

/**
 * A comment was added to a node (ADR-0014 шаг 1). Broadcast on the node's private
 * collaboration channel (channel_prefix.{node_id}) — the SAME room open editors join
 * (M4b) — so a live thread updates without a poll. Dispatched by the Action AFTER the
 * insert transaction commits.
 */
final readonly class CommentAdded implements ShouldBroadcast
{
    public string $eventId;

    public function __construct(
        public NodeComment $comment,
        ?string $eventId = null,
    ) {
        $this->eventId = $eventId ?? (string) Str::ulid();
    }

    /**
     * @return array<int, Channel>
     */
    public function broadcastOn(): array
    {
        return [
            new PrivateChannel(Config::channelPrefix().'.'.Identity::stringify($this->comment->node_id)),
        ];
    }

    public function broadcastAs(): string
    {
        return 'node-comment.added';
    }

    /**
     * @return array<string, mixed>
     */
    public function broadcastWith(): array
    {
        return [
            'id' => $this->comment->getKey(),
            'node_id' => $this->comment->node_id,
            'parent_id' => $this->comment->parent_id,
            'body' => $this->comment->body,
            'created_at' => $this->comment->created_at,
        ];
    }
}

        // default DefaultHostUserResolver; a host (or a test) may swap it. Purely
        // documents machinery — core neither defines nor binds it (D2 finding).
        $this->app->bind(HostUserResolver::class, DefaultHostUserResolver::class);
    }

    public function boot(): void
    {
        $this->registerBroadcastChannel();
    }

    /**
     * Authorize the private collaboration room channel (channel_prefix.{id}). The
     * room id is a NODE id (M4b): a kind=document node authorizes through the
     * Vaulter-owned AccessResolver (Ability::View to connect at all; read-only vs
     * writable is encoded in the issued session, not the channel). Gated on BOTH the
     * 'document_versions' feature AND 'collaboration' (VLT-REMED P3.1 / F-P1.6-01,
     * D13/D20) — the realtime channel is a separate opt-in over base document
     * editing. The channel preserves the broadcast authorization seam
     * independently of the Hocuspocus room token.
     */
    private function registerBroadcastChannel(): void
    {
        Broadcast::channel(
            Config::channelPrefix().'.{roomId}',
            static fn (Authenticatable $user, int|string $roomId): bool => Config::featureEnabled('document_versions')
                && Config::collaborationEnabled()
                && self::authorizeNodeRoom($user, $roomId),
        );
    }

    /**
     * Authorize a node room: the id resolves to a kind=document node the actor may at
     * least View through the AccessResolver.
     */
    private static function authorizeNodeRoom(Authenticatable $user, int|string $roomId): bool
    {
        if (!$user instanceof Authorizable) {
            return false;
        }

        $model = Config::nodeModel();
        $node = $model::query()->find($roomId);

        if (!$node instanceof Node || !$node->kind->isDocument()) {
            return false;
        }

        return app(AccessResolver::class)->can($user, Ability::View, $node);
    }
}

use Illuminate\Contracts\Events\ShouldDispatchAfterCommit;
use Illuminate\Support\Str;

/**
 * A node and its subtree were permanently soft-deleted (deleted_at set), their
 * version↔blob edges detached so the blobs become GC-eligible (M1b GC reclaims
 * the bytes — never deleted directly here, §2.4 / §2.3). used_bytes was
 * decremented by the freed live size. The node objects are gone, so only the ids
 * and the reclaimed byte total travel with the event.
 *
 * Dispatched inside the force-delete transaction, so — like every sibling Drive
 * event — it implements ShouldDispatchAfterCommit: listeners (GC scheduling,
 * notifications) only fire once the soft-delete + edge detach is durable, and
 * never on a rolled-back attempt.
 *
 * @property list<int|string> $nodeIds
 */
final readonly class NodePurged implements ShouldDispatchAfterCommit
{
    public string $eventId;

    /**
     * @param list<int|string> $nodeIds
     */
    public function __construct(
        public int|string $storageId,
        public array $nodeIds,
        public int $freedBytes,
        public int|string|null $actorId = null,
        ?string $eventId = null,
    ) {
        $this->eventId = $eventId ?? (string) Str::ulid();
    }
}

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace Vaulter\Drive\Uploads;

use Illuminate\Contracts\Container\Container;
use Illuminate\Support\Carbon;
use Illuminate\Support\Str;
use Illuminate\Validation\ValidationException;
use Symfony\Component\HttpKernel\Exception\TooManyRequestsHttpException;
use Vaulter\Database\VaulterDatabase;
use Vaulter\Drive\Contracts\Uploads\UploadProtocolHandler;
use Vaulter\Drive\Data\Uploads\InitiateUploadInput;
use Vaulter\Drive\Enums\Uploads\UploadProtocol;
use Vaulter\Drive\Enums\Uploads\UploadStatus;
use Vaulter\Drive\Events\Uploads\UploadAborted;
use Vaulter\Drive\Events\Uploads\UploadExpired;
use Vaulter\Drive\Events\Uploads\UploadInitiated;
use Vaulter\Drive\Exceptions\Uploads\UploadConflictException;
use Vaulter\Drive\Models\Uploads\UploadSession;
use Vaulter\Drive\Repositories\Uploads\UploadSessionReadRepository;
use Vaulter\Drive\Repositories\Uploads\UploadSessionStoreRepository;
use Vaulter\Support\Config;

/**
 * The resumable-upload lifecycle coordinator (§2.8 / D16 / M3a). It owns:
 *   - initiate(UploadInitData) → a fresh UploadSession (status=initiated, a UNIQUE
 *     upload_id, expires_at = now + the configured TTL), oversize-rejected up front;
 *   - the lifecycle transitions (initiated → uploading → assembled → committed) plus
 *     abort/expire, each guarded by UploadStatus::canTransitionTo;
 *   - resolving the per-protocol handler (TusUploadHandler / S3MultipartHandler) for
 *     a session.
 *
 * It is read/CLI-context safe: it takes no Request and persists through the store
 * repository (never Model::create) so the controller stays thin and the sweeper /
 * queue can drive it. The actual assemble→commit (BlobStore.commit) is
 * CommitUploadAction — the manager only moves the session's state and cleans up the
 * staged temp + protocol state on abort/expire (H.3).
 */
final readonly class UploadSessionManager
{
    public function __construct(
        private Container $container,
        private UploadSessionStoreRepository $sessions,
        private UploadSessionReadRepository $sessionsRead,
        private StagedUpload $staged,
        private VaulterDatabase $database,
    ) {}

    /**
     * Open a resumable session (§2.8). Validates the declared total against the
     * configured ceiling BEFORE any bytes are accepted (oversize rejected up front,
     * never staged), checks the actor's active-session cap (P1.3 / F-P1.4-09), mints
     * a UNIQUE upload_id, stamps the TTL, and lets the protocol handler initialise
     * its side (S3 CreateMultipartUpload; a no-op for tus).
     */
    public function initiate(InitiateUploadInput $data): UploadSession
    {
        $this->assertWithinMaxBytes($data->totalSizeBytes);
        $this->assertWithinActiveSessionCap($data->actorId);

        $session = $this->sessions->create([
            'tenant_id' => $this->tenantId($data),
            'drive_id' => $data->storage->getKey(),
            'upload_id' => (string) Str::uuid(),
            'target_node_id' => $data->targetNode?->getKey(),
            'target_parent_id' => $data->targetParent?->getKey(),
            'target_name' => $data->targetName,
            'protocol' => $data->protocol,
            'status' => UploadStatus::Initiated,
            'expected_sha256' => $data->expectedSha256,
            'total_size_bytes' => $data->totalSizeBytes,
            'received_bytes' => 0,
            'chunk_size' => Config::uploadChunkSize(),
            'mime_type' => $data->mimeType,
            'metadata' => $data->metadata === [] ? null : $data->metadata,
            'expires_at' => Carbon::now()->addHours(Config::uploadSessionTtlHours()),
            'created_by' => $data->actorId,
        ]);

title: Configuration reference
description: Exhaustive reference for every config/vaulter.php key — defaults, env vars, and accepted values.
outline: deep
---

# Configuration reference

Every key in `config/vaulter.php`, by section. Publish the file with:
10→
```bash
php artisan vendor:publish --tag=vaulter-config
```

Each table column: the config path (relative to `vaulter.`), the env override (when
one exists), the shipped default, and what it controls. Values are read back through
the `Vaulter\Support\Config` helper, which the package uses everywhere instead of raw
`config()` calls.

20→::: warning Config-cache safe
Every binding is an FQCN or a plain scalar — no closures. The config is safe to
`php artisan config:cache`.
:::

## Models — `models.*`

Swappable Eloquent models. Point any entry at your own subclass to add behaviour
(ULID keys, tenant scoping, audit). Vaulter always resolves models through this map.

30→| Key | Default | Owned by |
|---|---|---|
| `models.storage` | `Vaulter\Models\Drive\Drive` | core |
| `models.node` | `Vaulter\Models\Drive\Node` | core |
| `models.file` | `Vaulter\Models\Drive\File` | core |
| `models.file_version` | `Vaulter\Models\Drive\FileRevision` | core |
| `models.blob` | `Vaulter\Models\Cas\Blob` | core |
| `models.file_version_blob` | `Vaulter\Models\Drive\FileRevisionBlob` | core |
| `models.grant` | `Vaulter\Models\Access\NodeGrant` | core |
| `models.node_share` | `Vaulter\Models\Sharing\NodeShare` | core |
40→| `models.upload_session` | `Vaulter\Drive\Models\Uploads\UploadSession` | `axioma-studio/vaulter-drive` |
| `models.upload_part` | `Vaulter\Drive\Models\Uploads\UploadPart` | `axioma-studio/vaulter-drive` |
| `models.node_comment` | `Vaulter\Documents\Models\Comments\NodeComment` | `axioma-studio/vaulter-documents` |
| `models.node_document_version` | `Vaulter\Documents\Models\Revisions\DocumentRevision` | `axioma-studio/vaulter-documents` |
| `models.activity` | `Vaulter\Models\Activity\Activity` | core |
| `models.outbox` | `Vaulter\Models\Webhooks\Outbox` | core |
| `models.webhook_endpoint` | `Vaulter\Models\Webhooks\WebhookEndpoint` | core |
| `models.webhook_delivery` | `Vaulter\Models\Webhooks\WebhookDelivery` | core |

::: info Package-owned models resolve only when the package is installed
50→`upload_session` / `upload_part` are merged into `vaulter.models` by
`axioma-studio/vaulter-drive`; `node_comment` / `node_document_version` are merged by
`axioma-studio/vaulter-documents`. Core ships **no default** for these four keys —
resolving them without the owning package installed throws. The legacy
document-id-attached models (`document`, `version`, `folder`, `permission`, `comment`,
`share`) were fully excised — see [ADR-0014](/adr/0014-legacy-docvault-strangler).
:::

## Table names — `table_names.*`

60→Base table name per entity, resolved as `{table_prefix}{base}`. Rename a single
entity's table here without changing the global prefix.

| Key | Default base |
|---|---|
| `table_names.storages` | `storages` |
| `table_names.nodes` | `nodes` |
| `table_names.blobs` | `blobs` |
| `table_names.files` | `files` |
| `table_names.file_versions` | `file_versions` |
70→| `table_names.file_version_blobs` | `file_version_blobs` |
| `table_names.node_grants` | `node_grants` |
| `table_names.node_shares` | `node_shares` |
| `table_names.node_comments` | `node_comments` |
| `table_names.node_document_versions` | `node_document_versions` |
| `table_names.upload_sessions` | `upload_sessions` |
| `table_names.upload_parts` | `upload_parts` |
| `table_names.activity` | `activity` |
| `table_names.outbox` | `outbox` |
| `table_names.webhook_endpoints` | `webhook_endpoints` |
80→| `table_names.webhook_deliveries` | `webhook_deliveries` |

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

// The drive package is strict-typed end to end.
arch('strict types')
    ->expect('Vaulter\Drive')
    ->toUseStrictTypes();

// T11 — drive and documents are independent siblings over core: nothing under
// Vaulter\Drive may reach into the documents engine. The Drive node read shape that
// embedded the document handler descriptor moved to core (Http\Resources\Drive\
// NodeResource) precisely so this stays true.
arch('drive never depends on documents')
    ->expect('Vaulter\Drive')
    ->not->toUse('Vaulter\Documents');

// E5.1 / F-P4.3-01 — declarative form kept for discoverability/grep (`toUse('App')`);
// see the file-scan test below (and core's ArchTest.php) for why this namespace-graph
// form cannot itself observe a real "uses" edge in this dev/test environment.
arch('the package never depends on the host application (E5.1)')
    ->expect('Vaulter\Drive')
    ->not->toUse('App');

/**
 * E5.1 / F-P4.3-01 — vaulter-drive is an embeddable Laravel package: it must never
 * reach into the HOST application's namespace. File scan (not
 * `expect(...)->not->toUse('App')`) because `App\*` is never an autoloadable class in
 * the package's own dev/test environment (red-before proven on core's ArchTest.php).
 */
test('non-test src never references the host App namespace (E5.1, F-P4.3-01)', function (): void {
    $src = __DIR__.'/../../src';
    $offenders = [];

    /** @var Iterator<SplFileInfo> $files */
    $files = new RegexIterator(
        new RecursiveIteratorIterator(new RecursiveDirectoryIterator($src)),
        '/\.php$/',
    );

    foreach ($files as $file) {
        $contents = file_get_contents($file->getPathname());

        if ($contents === false) {
            continue;
        }

        $code = '';

        foreach (token_get_all($contents) as $token) {
            if (is_array($token) && in_array($token[0], [T_COMMENT, T_DOC_COMMENT], true)) {
                continue;
            }

            $code .= is_array($token) ? $token[1] : $token;
        }

        if (preg_match('/\\bApp\\\\/', $code) === 1) {
            $offenders[] = $file->getPathname();
        }
    }

    expect($offenders)->toBe([]);
});

/**
 * ADR-0017 / VLT-REMED P4.9 + P4.10 — Canon A, Law 1 (layer-first placement).
 *
 * `drive` was DIVERGENT: the `Uploads/` module carried its own nested layer tree
 * (`Uploads/Actions`, `Uploads/Models`, `Uploads/Repositories`, `Uploads/Http`,
 * `Uploads/Enums`, `Uploads/Data`, `Uploads/Contracts`) — a layer nested UNDER a
 * domain, the inverse of the core canon. P4.10 DISCHARGED it: those layer
 * subtrees were dissolved into the package-root layers with an `Uploads` domain
 * sub-namespace (`Actions/Uploads`, `Models/Uploads`, `Repositories/Uploads`,
 * `Enums/Uploads`, `Data/Uploads`, `Contracts/Uploads`, `Http/<sub>/Uploads`); the
 * flat upload service classes stayed as the `Uploads/` domain-service folder
 * (mirrors `core/src/Sharing`). This test now asserts the CANON and passes GREEN;
 * the `->todo()` was removed by P4.10.
 *
 * Red-before proven (P4.9): before the move, this body failed with offenders
 * `Uploads/Actions`, `Uploads/Contracts`, `Uploads/Data`, `Uploads/Enums`,
 * `Uploads/Http`, `Uploads/Http/Controllers`, `Uploads/Http/Requests`,
 * `Uploads/Http/Resources`, `Uploads/Models`, `Uploads/Repositories`.
 *
 * VLT-CANON P2.3 further split the `Uploads/` domain-service folder by role:
 * `*Handler`/`*Manager` orchestrators (`TusUploadHandler`, `S3MultipartHandler`,
 * `UploadSessionManager`) stayed; the pure helpers (`MagicByteSniffer`,
 * `StagedUpload`, `UploadModels`) moved to `Support/Uploads` — still outside the
 * `$layers` list below, so this test is unaffected.
 */
test('technical layers are never nested under a domain module (ADR-0017 Law 1)', function (): void {
    $src = __DIR__.'/../../src';
    $layers = ['Actions', 'Models', 'Repositories', 'Enums', 'Events', 'Data', 'Contracts', 'Http'];
    $offenders = [];

    // SELF_FIRST so DIRECTORIES are yielded (the default LEAVES_ONLY mode only
    // yields files, which would make this dir-structure check an inert no-op).
    /** @var Iterator<SplFileInfo> $dirs */
    $dirs = new RecursiveIteratorIterator(
        new RecursiveDirectoryIterator($src, FilesystemIterator::SKIP_DOTS),
        RecursiveIteratorIterator::SELF_FIRST,
    );

    foreach ($dirs as $dir) {
        if (!$dir->isDir()) {
            continue;
        }

        $relative = str_replace($src.'/', '', $dir->getPathname());
        $segments = explode('/', $relative);

        foreach ($segments as $index => $segment) {
            if ($index > 0 && in_array($segment, $layers, true)) {
                $offenders[] = $relative;
                break;
            }
        }
    }

    expect(array_values(array_unique($offenders)))->toBe([]);

content.text:
70→  a missing destination always resolves to the root.
- **Destinations are live folders of the same drive.** Creating, uploading, moving or
  copying into a file, a document or a trashed folder raises
  `InvalidDestinationException` (409 `invalid_destination`); a folder of another drive
  raises `CrossDriveOperationException` (409 `cross_drive_operation`).
- **The root is never an operand.** Renaming, moving, copying, trashing or
  force-deleting it raises `InvalidDestinationException`.
- **No cycles.** A folder cannot move into itself or its own subtree
  (`NodeCycleException`, 409 `node_move_cycle`), even when two moves race.

80→Every write takes the drive's tree lock first — exclusively for move, restore, trash and
force-delete, shared for create, upload, copy and rename — and only then locks node rows.
On PostgreSQL uploads into one drive stay concurrent; a structural operation waits for
them. A custom Action that changes the tree should follow the same order
(`VaulterDatabase::lockTree()` / `lockTreeShared()`, then node rows).

```php
$root = $drive->root();          // Vaulter\Models\Drive\Node
$storage = $drive->model();    // Vaulter\Models\Drive\Drive
$profile = $drive->profile();  // Vaulter\Profiles\Profile
90→$profileId = $profile->getId(); // string
```

### Quota & usage

The storage tracks `used_bytes` and an optional `quota_bytes` (nullable = no
quota). Both are integer-cast on the model and surfaced verbatim by the
[`DriveResource`](/reference/rest-api#storages) so the UI can render a usage bar:

```php
100→$storage = $drive->model();

$storage->used_bytes;   // int — bytes currently consumed
$storage->quota_bytes;  // ?int — null means unlimited
```

::: info `used_bytes` is maintained by the Drive
`used_bytes` is advanced/released by the upload and force-delete Actions (a purge
detaches the version↔blob edges and releases the quota). There is no public
"set quota" method on the handle — set `quota_bytes` on the storage model directly,

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace Vaulter\Documents\Providers;

use Spatie\LaravelPackageTools\Package;

final class HttpRegistrar
{
    public function configure(Package $package): void
    {
        $package->hasRoute('documents');
    }
}

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace Vaulter\Drive\Providers;

use Illuminate\Contracts\Events\Dispatcher;
use Illuminate\Contracts\Foundation\Application;
use Spatie\LaravelPackageTools\Package;
use Vaulter\Drive\Activity\RecordsDriveActivity;
use Vaulter\Drive\Console\PurgeTrashCommand;
use Vaulter\Drive\Console\SweepUploadsCommand;
use Vaulter\Drive\Webhooks\RecordsDriveOutbox;
use Vaulter\Support\Config;

final class HttpRegistrar
{
    public function configure(Package $package): void
    {
        $package
            ->hasRoute('drive')
            ->hasCommand(PurgeTrashCommand::class)
            ->hasCommand(SweepUploadsCommand::class);
    }

    public function boot(Application $app): void
    {
        if (Config::featureEnabled('activity')) {
            $app->make(Dispatcher::class)->subscribe(RecordsDriveActivity::class);
        }

        if (Config::featureEnabled('reliability')) {
            $app->make(Dispatcher::class)->subscribe(RecordsDriveOutbox::class);
        }
    }
}

1→# Changelog

All notable changes to **Vaulter** will be documented in this file.

The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/),
and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).

## [Unreleased]

10→### Changed

- Document classes now use revisions, canonical Action/Input names and domain controller namespaces (AD03, AD04). Documents registration is split into independently tested bindings, HTTP and collaboration registrars.

- Drive classes use canonical names and domain namespaces; DriveHandle exposes
  `model(): Drive` and `profile(): Profile` through its core interface, and the
  provider delegates to tested registrars (AD03, AD04). Unused WorkspaceRef and
  BulkAction removed; see UPGRADE.md for the FQN migration map.

- Canonical 0.3 schema and upgrade migrations №1, №2, №4, №8, №9: drives,
20→  file revisions, ordinary grant uniqueness, event and subscription conversion;
  fresh tables are independent of runtime features (P2.7; see UPGRADE.md).

- Canonical core API: Storage → Drive, FileVersion → FileRevision, Panels → Profiles,
  HostRoleDriver/PermissionResolver → PermissionDriver, Engines → Handlers; no PHP aliases
  (AD03, AD04; see UPGRADE.md for the complete FQN map).
- File handlers use vendor/name `key()` and `viewer()`; viewer descriptors expose key/props,
  and `NodePresenter::present()` replaces `describe()` (AD14).
- Activity and webhook enums merged into EventType with canonical 0.3 values;
  webhook subscriptions exclude upload lifecycle events (AD03, AD04).
30→- Core provider delegates to five registrars; own-tables profile API and hooks, including
  the previously invoked booted(), removed. Profile scaffolding is vaulter:make:profile
  (AD05, AD11). Configuration key normalization follows in P2.5.


### Added
- `BlobStore::commitStaged()` for quota-first uploads and reusable staging across SQL retries (AD21).
- Lossless `BlobScope`, `scope_key`, upgrade migration №7 and resumable
  `vaulter:blobs:repair-scopes --dry-run|--execute` (AD20).
- Batch ACL evaluation (`AccessResolver::evaluateMany`, `AclFolder`), `NodePage`,
40→  `ExactListing`, signed query-bound cursors and `listing.scan_budget` (AD12).

 * The read shape of a storage container (§2.1): its meta, the root node the
 * client opens into, and the used/quota accounting the UI shows as a usage bar.
 * Read-only — it transforms an already-loaded Storage, never WRITES (it resolves the

 *
 * @mixin Drive

    /**

    #[\Override]

        /** @var Drive $storage */
        $storage = $this->resource;

        return [
            'id' => $storage->getKey(),
            'panel' => $storage->profile,
            'owner' => [
                'type' => $storage->owner_type,
                'id' => $storage->owner_id,
            ],
            'name' => $storage->name,
            'slug' => null,
            'root_node_id' => $storage->root_node_id,
            'disk' => $storage->disk,
            'storage_type' => null,
            'used_bytes' => $storage->used_bytes,
            'quota_bytes' => $storage->quota_bytes,
            'status' => $storage->status,
            'created_at' => $storage->created_at,
            'updated_at' => $storage->updated_at,
            // What the request actor may do on the storage ROOT (§2.6 / H.2),
            // resolved through the AccessResolver so the Vue client gates its
            // toolbar (open the storage, create folders, upload, manage).
            'abilities' => $this->abilities($request, $storage),
        ];
    }

     * the AccessResolver for the request's actor (§2.6 / H.2). Mapped to the four
     * frontend keys: view (View on root), create_folder + upload (Create on root,
     * AND the workspace-create gate), manage (Manage on root).
     *
     * Resilience: with no acting user OR no provisioned root node yet, every flag is
     * false — a read-only shell (the SAFE default; the toolbar advertises nothing it
     * cannot back). The Resource never WRITES, so a missing root is resolved as
     * "nothing yet", never auto-provisioned here.
     *

1→# Error Reference

Every Vaulter exception extends `Vaulter\Exceptions\VaulterException` and carries a
message in the form `[Vaulter] {what}. Why: {…}. Fix: {…}. Docs: {url}` where the URL
points at the matching anchor below.

## domain-http-errors

Domain exceptions implement `Vaulter\Exceptions\Contracts\ProblemException`.
10→For JSON requests or routes under the configured Vaulter prefix, the response is
`{message, code}` with the following HTTP status. HTML requests to host routes and
configuration/infrastructure exceptions use Laravel's normal exception handler.
Codes are a stable public contract (AD29).

| Code | HTTP | Exception |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `permission_denied` | 403 | `Vaulter\Exceptions\Access\PermissionDeniedException` |
| `node_name_conflict` | 409 | `Vaulter\Exceptions\Nodes\NodeNameConflictException` |
| `node_move_cycle` | 409 | `Vaulter\Drive\Exceptions\Nodes\NodeCycleException` |
20→| `cross_drive_operation` | 409 | `Vaulter\Drive\Exceptions\Nodes\CrossDriveOperationException` |
| `invalid_destination` | 409 | `Vaulter\Exceptions\Nodes\InvalidDestinationException` |
| `node_not_trashed` | 409 | `Vaulter\Exceptions\Nodes\NodeNotTrashedException` |
| `quota_exceeded` | 413 | `Vaulter\Drive\Exceptions\Quota\QuotaExceededException` |
| `upload_conflict` | 409 | `Vaulter\Drive\Exceptions\Uploads\UploadConflictException` |
| `upload_conflict` | 409 | `Vaulter\Drive\Exceptions\Uploads\StagedUploadMissingException` |
| `upload_offset_mismatch` | 409 | `Vaulter\Drive\Exceptions\Uploads\OffsetMismatchException` |
| `upload_rejected` | 422 | `Vaulter\Drive\Exceptions\Uploads\UploadContentMismatchException` |
| `not_a_document` | 409 | `Vaulter\Documents\Exceptions\NotADocumentException` |
| `unknown_document_type` | 422 | `Vaulter\Documents\Exceptions\UnknownDocumentTypeException` |
30→| `invalid_document_content` | 422 | `Vaulter\Documents\Exceptions\InvalidDocumentContentException` |
| `document_revision_not_found` | 404 | `Vaulter\Documents\Exceptions\DocumentRevisionNotFoundException` |
| `unknown_export_format` | 422 | `Vaulter\Exceptions\Documents\UnknownExportFormatException` |
| `invalid_document_content` | 422 | `Vaulter\Exceptions\Documents\UnsupportedDocumentContentException` |
| `validation_failed` | 422 | `Vaulter\Exceptions\Nodes\InvalidNodeNameException` |
| `validation_failed` | 422 | `Vaulter\Exceptions\Webhooks\BlockedOutboundUrlException` |
| `validation_failed` | 422 | `Vaulter\Exceptions\Access\UnenumerableGrantSubjectException` |
| `unknown_profile` | 422 | `Vaulter\Exceptions\Profiles\UnknownProfileException` |
| `node_not_found` | 404 | `Vaulter\Exceptions\Nodes\NodeNotFoundException` |
| `drive_not_found` | 404 | `Vaulter\Exceptions\Nodes\StorageNotFoundException` |
40→
The response also preserves `errors.name` for name conflicts and invalid names, `errors.url` for blocked
outbound URLs and `errors.subject_type` for unenumerable grant subjects. Content errors
include `reason`: `mime_mismatch`, `invalid_tiptap` or `unsupported_content`.
Offset mismatches include `Upload-Offset` and `Tus-Resumable: 1.0.0` headers.

## node-not-found

`NodeNotFoundException::forId()` — the node does not exist or is not visible to the
current actor in the current drive/tenant. These cases use the same 404 response.

content.text:
1→# Справочник ошибок

Каждое исключение Vaulter наследуется от `Vaulter\Exceptions\VaulterException` и несёт
сообщение в формате `[Vaulter] {what}. Why: {…}. Fix: {…}. Docs: {url}`, где URL
указывает на соответствующий якорь ниже.

## document-not-found

`DocumentNotFoundException` — запрошенный id документа не существует, был мягко удалён
10→или лежит вне текущего workspace. Проверьте id и фильтр по workspace. API отображает
это на `404`.

## permission-denied

`PermissionDeniedException` — ваш `PermissionResolver` вернул `false` для запрошенного
действия. Выдайте нужный уровень доступа или поправьте resolver. API отображает это на `403`.

## unknown-document-type

20→`UnknownDocumentTypeException` — переданный `type` отсутствует в
`config('vaulter.enabled_document_types')`. Включите его или зарегистрируйте свой тип через
`Vaulter::registerDocumentType()`.

## invalid-tiptap-content

`InvalidDocumentContentException::missingDocNode()` — корень контента должен быть
`{"type":"doc", …}`. Передайте валидный TipTap-документ в JSON или используйте `TipTapContent::empty()`.

## content-too-large
30→
`InvalidDocumentContentException::tooLarge()` — контент превышает
`config('vaulter.max_document_size_kb')`. Разбейте документ или поднимите лимит.

## unknown-collaboration-driver

`VaulterException` из `Vaulter::driver()` — указанный драйвер не зарегистрирован в
`config('vaulter.collaboration.drivers')`. Добавьте запись, чей `class` реализует
`CollaborationDriver`.

40→## missing-jwt

Драйверу Hocuspocus нужен `firebase/php-jwt`, чтобы выпускать токены комнат. Выполните
`composer require firebase/php-jwt`.

## missing-collab-secret

`UploadProtocol` (`Vaulter\Enums\Uploads\UploadProtocol`) selects the transport per session:

| Protocol      | Value           | Works on | How |
| ------------- | --------------- | -------- | --- |
| **tus**       | `tus`           | **any** Flysystem disk | tus.io CORE — Creation + `HEAD`(`Upload-Offset`) + `PATCH`(`application/offset+octet-stream`). Each chunk is appended to a staged temp; `received_bytes` is the authoritative offset. |
| **S3 multipart** | `s3-multipart` | S3-style disks | Numbered parts recorded in `v_upload_parts` (re-upload of a part replaces it), stitched on complete. |
| **Direct**    | `direct`        | any | A one-shot non-resumable `POST` — the small-file fast path. |

The default is **tus** (the disk-agnostic resumable path). The transport is chosen at session
50→create time; the `UploadSessionManager` resolves the matching handler (`TusUploadHandler` /
`S3MultipartHandler`) from the container, so a host can swap either implementation.

## Session lifecycle

A resumable upload is a first-class row (`UploadSession`, `v_upload_sessions`). `UploadStatus`
drives the state machine:

```
Initiated → Uploading → Assembled → Committed

Use this skill whenever the user wants to create or change a Google Doc, Sheet or Slides file in their Google Drive. Triggers include: a request that names Google Docs, Sheets, Slides or Drive and asks to make, edit, format, copy or rename a file; a docs.google.com link with a request to change that file, even a one-line fix or suggested edits; and any follow-up change to a Google file from earlier in the chat, even "change it" or "add a tab". Includes helper scripts for document positions, cell ranges and slide layout. However, if the user asks for a doc, deck or spreadsheet without naming Google, or gives a Google file only as source material for something new, use Claude's own output type instead. Do NOT use for read-only questions about a Google file, or for Word, Excel, PowerPoint or PDF files.

35→reusing the staged object, then discards it in `finally`. If SQL fails after physical
promotion, the bytes form an orphan collected by `vaulter:reconcile-blobs --orphans
--prune` after grace. Reconciliation keeps committed winners' bytes.

## Transports
40→
`UploadProtocol` (`Vaulter\Enums\Uploads\UploadProtocol`) selects the transport per session:

| Protocol      | Value           | Works on | How |
| ------------- | --------------- | -------- | --- |
| **tus**       | `tus`           | **any** Flysystem disk | tus.io CORE — Creation + `HEAD`(`Upload-Offset`) + `PATCH`(`application/offset+octet-stream`). Each chunk is appended to a staged temp; `received_bytes` is the authoritative offset. |
| **S3 multipart** | `s3-multipart` | S3-style disks | Numbered parts recorded in `v_upload_parts` (re-upload of a part replaces it), stitched on complete. |

promotion, the bytes form an orphan collected by `vaulter:reconcile-blobs --orphans
--prune` after grace. Reconciliation keeps committed winners' bytes.

## Transports

`UploadProtocol` (`Vaulter\Enums\Uploads\UploadProtocol`) selects the transport per session:

| Protocol      | Value           | Works on | How |
| ------------- | --------------- | -------- | --- |
| **tus**       | `tus`           | **any** Flysystem disk | tus.io CORE — Creation + `HEAD`(`Upload-Offset`) + `PATCH`(`application/offset+octet-stream`). Each chunk is appended to a staged temp; `received_bytes` is the authoritative offset. |
| **S3 multipart** | `s3-multipart` | S3-style disks | Numbered parts recorded in `v_upload_parts` (re-upload of a part replaces it), stitched on complete. |

1→<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace Vaulter\Drive\Enums\Uploads;

use Vaulter\Attributes\Label;
use Vaulter\Support\Concerns\HasLabel;

10→/**
 * The resumable-upload transport a session speaks (master plan §2.8 / D16):
 *
 *  - Tus         — the tus.io CORE protocol (Creation + HEAD(Upload-Offset) +
 *                  PATCH(application/offset+octet-stream)). Each PATCH chunk is
 *                  appended to a staged temp on the session's disk; received_bytes
 *                  is the authoritative offset. Works on ANY Flysystem disk.
 *  - S3Multipart — the object-store multipart protocol: initiate on the bucket,
 *                  hand back presigned part URLs (or proxy PUT each part), record
 *                  parts in v_upload_parts, complete-multipart, then feed the
20→ *                  assembled object to BlobStore (server recompute sha256 — never
 *                  trust the multipart ETag, H.3). Only on S3-style disks.
 *  - Direct      — a one-shot (non-resumable) PUT; the session is a thin envelope
 *                  whose bytes are staged and committed in a single step (the
 *                  small-file fast path; reserved).
 */

availableCommands.description: Read this before the first Google Drive, Docs, Sheets or Slides connector call whenever the task creates or changes a Google file. Use this skill whenever the user wants to create or change a Google Doc, Sheet or Slides file in their Google Drive. Triggers include: a request that names Google Docs, Sheets, Slides or Drive and asks to make, edit, format, copy or rename a file; a docs.google.com link with a request to change that file, even a one-line fix or suggested edits; and any follow-up change to a Google file from earlier in the chat, even "change it" or "add a tab". Includes helper scripts for document positions, cell ranges and slide layout. However, if the user asks for a doc, deck or spreadsheet without naming Google, or gives a Google file only as source material for something new, use Claude's own output type instead. Do NOT use for read-only questions about a Google file, or for Word, Excel, PowerPoint or PDF files.
